status_summary: USAID closed on 2025-07-01 with its remaining operations merged into State, and GAO reported that USAID staff fell from about 13,600 in January 2025 to 241 in April 2026, so the text's USAID-specific staffing plan (a political Chief Human Capital Officer and General Counsel attorneys, a Schedule F pilot, an SES mobility program, a Day One training replacement, a Senior Accountable Official and targeted recruiting) was not carried out as such, and no such step was found. Related government-wide steps run in the same direction: OPM published a final rule on 2026-02-06 (effective 2026-03-09) creating Schedule Policy/Career, the successor to Schedule F, and NPR reported in March 2025 that a political appointee serving as USAID Deputy Administrator signed the program cancellations. Because the wind-down moved toward, not against, political control of the workforce, the record is judged not_started with a parallel match rather than diverged. Litigation over the dismantling continues, with a D.C. Circuit appeal argued on 2026-04-23 and no ruling reported by early October 2026.

timeline.event: A federal judge extended a temporary restraining order, to 2025-02-21, blocking USAID from placing more employees on paid administrative leave, in a suit by AFSA and AFGE; more than 2,000 staff were already locked out of headquarters and systems.

NPR reported that a political appointee serving as USAID Deputy Administrator and State Director of Foreign Assistance signed orders cancelling about 5,200 programs, with directives aiming to shrink the workforce to a couple of hundred people.

Government Executive reported that nearly all USAID positions not required by law would be eliminated through reductions in force effective 2025-07-01 or 2025-09-02, that employees could choose leave from 2025-03-29, and that a circuit court on Friday 2025-03-28 suspended a district court's 2025-03-18 pause on the dismantling (the Fourth Circuit, per Nexstar).
NPR reported that USAID officially shut down and its remaining operations merged into State.
OPM published a final rule (91 FR 5580, effective 2026-03-09) creating Schedule Policy/Career, the government-wide successor to Schedule F; it applies across agencies, not as a USAID pilot.

The D.C. Circuit heard argument, mainly on jurisdiction, in the appeal of AFGE v. Trump (No. 25-5290), the challenge to dismantling USAID; AFSA's tracker (updated 2026-10-07) reports no ruling, and says the Fourth Circuit stay of the injunction in J. Doe 4 v. Musk remains with the case in discovery.

GAO reported USAID staffing fell from about 13,600 in January 2025 to 241 in April 2026, and that of 7,510 USAID awards about 730 remained active in March 2026, with responsibility for them transferred to State.

title: Staff USAID with political appointees, a Schedule F pilot and day-one policy training
uncertainties: Searches recorded by the researcher for a USAID chief human capital officer, Schedule C or Administratively Determined hiring, General Counsel attorney appointments, a Schedule F pilot, SES mobility program, Day One training halt and Senior Accountable Official found nothing specific; this review did not repeat them. Whether Schedule Policy/Career placements under Executive Order 14410 include foreign assistance positions at State was not checked; the government-wide program is tracked in c03-01. The stage is a judgment call: the closure is materially different from a restaffed agency, which a broad reading would treat as diverged, but it does not run against the text's aim of political control of the workforce. The Fourth Circuit stay date of 2025-03-28 rests on the Government Executive report of that date. GAO does not state how many USAID staff moved to State. The NPR article names the individual; this record uses office titles only. Overlap with c09-01 is partial: c09-01 covers the Director of Foreign Assistance structure and the agency's fate.
